name: Ceftriaxone
status: PILOT – † lines checked against package insert 2026-11-15; awaiting review

pi_source.title: Ceftriaxone 500 mg / 1 g FKSA (Fresenius Kabi) – professional information (SAHPRA repository, Aug 2024)

dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not stated in the package insert consulted
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page (s=pi: package insert), d=dagger, n=from own notes, b=bold, h=heading
summary: Broad-spectrum parenteral cephalosporin with once-daily dosing and good CSF penetration; used for meningitis, sepsis, severe pneumonia, pyelonephritis and gonococcal infection.

forms.t: Powder for injection: 500 mg, 1 g and 2 g vials (250 mg vials from other suppliers)

moa.t: β-lactam: binds transpeptidase and blocks the last step of bacterial cell-wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis → cell lysis
Bactericidal; stable to most penicillinases and cephalosporinases
Inherently resistant: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, enterococci, Listeria, MRSA, and atypicals (Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, Legionella)

pk.t: Half-life about 8 hours in adults; 2–3 times longer in infants under 8 days
CSF concentration averages 17% of plasma in bacterial meningitis
Excreted unchanged: 50–60% in urine, 40–50% in bile

items.t: PHC before referral: 2 g IM immediately (max 1 g per injection site); repeat after 12 hours if referral is delayed
Severe acute malnutrition: 100 mg/kg/dose once daily; 80 mg/kg/dose if meningitis suspected
Other indications use 50–80 mg/kg once daily (e.g. epiglottitis 50 mg/kg, bacterial tracheitis 80 mg/kg) – see the pathway

dosing.h: Young infant – first dose before referral

items.t: 50 mg/kg IM; dilute a 250 mg vial with 1 mL sterile water
Neonates: daily dose should not exceed 50 mg/kg
1 g IV daily for 48 hours or until fever subsides, then oral step-down
1–2 g IV daily depending on indication (wound sepsis 2 g daily; typhoid 2 g 12 hourly) – see the pathway
Hospital STG syndromic: 1 g IM single dose; dissolve 1 g in 3.6 mL lidocaine 1% without adrenaline
PID and PHC STG: 250 mg IM single dose
< 12 years: 125 mg IM single dose; > 12 years: 250 mg IM single dose

administration.t: Do not inject more than 1 g IM at one site
IV injection over 2–4 minutes; IV infusion over at least 30 minutes (60 minutes in neonates)
IM: reconstitute 1 g in 3.5 mL water for injection or lidocaine 1%; the lidocaine solution must never be given IV
Never mix or give simultaneously with calcium-containing IV solutions (e.g. Ringer's lactate), at any age
≤ 28 days old: no calcium-containing IV fluids for 48 hours after ceftriaxone
> 28 days old: may give sequentially if the giving set is flushed with sodium chloride 0.9% before and after
Incompatible in the same line with aminoglycosides, vancomycin and fluconazole

adjustments.t: No reduction if hepatic function is intact; creatinine clearance < 10 mL/minute: max 2 g daily
No reduction if renal function is intact
Excreted in breast milk in low concentration; use with caution

contraindications.t: Hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone or any cephalosporin
Previous severe hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylaxis) to any other β-lactam, including penicillins
Penicillin allergy that is not severe is not a contraindication; avoid only if documented cephalosporin anaphylaxis
Premature neonates up to 41 weeks postmenstrual age
Term neonates (≤ 28 days) with jaundice, hypoalbuminaemia or acidosis, or who need IV calcium

cautions.t: Own notes record about 20% cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy; guideline position above
Displaces bilirubin from albumin – risk of bilirubin encephalopathy in neonates

adverse_effects.t: Gallbladder precipitation (appears as gallstones on ultrasound); pseudomembranous colitis (C. difficile)

monitoring.t: Review at 48–72 hours with cultures; step down to oral when clinically appropriate

conflicts.t: Neonatal jaundice: the package insert contraindicates ceftriaxone in jaundiced neonates; the PHC STG says give it even if jaundiced when serious bacterial infection is suspected. The pathway follows the STG.
Pregnancy: the package insert says it should not be used in pregnancy (safety not established); the STG and maternity guideline use it for pyelonephritis and wound sepsis.
